We evaluate the framework on mixtures of ImageNet-C corruptions using convolution-based (ConvNeXtV2-Femto), self-attention-based (DeiT-Tiny), and hybrid (TinyViT-5M) vision models, on person classification (Visual Wake Words), and on object detection (MS-COCO). Our results reveal that adaptation driven solely by the transmitted descriptors recovers $93-95\%$ of the supervised oracle adaptation gain on all three architectures, $82\%$ on Visual Wake Words and $94$--$98\%$ on MS-COCO. Notably, adaptation quality degrades gracefully as the descriptor resolution decreases from $224 $ to $28$ pixels, consistently across architectures, enabling bandwidth reductions from $213\times$ to $784\times$ across the frequency descriptors. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Watch Your Step: Anticipated Perception for Humanoid Locomotion
docs.text:
Watch Your Step: Anticipated Perception for Humanoid Locomotion Watch Your Step: Anticipated Perception for Humanoid Locomotion arXiv:2610.29612v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Perceptive locomotion policies typically observe a dense robot-centric elevation map, although only the terrain beneath and around the next footsteps informs the control decision. Learned encoders compress the whole visual input, leaving the policy to work out which inputs matter while learning the baseline locomotion task. Learning both at once slows training and, without computationally expensive attention mechanisms, makes generalization to new terrain harder. We instead remove redundant inputs from the elevation map before the policy sees it. A lightweight foothold prediction model (FPM) predicts future footholds from proprioception and the velocity command alone, and we sample the elevation map only in small patches around these predicted footholds. We train the prediction model alongside the locomotion policy, periodically retraining it on new policy rollouts as the robot's gait matures. This allows the perception to anticipate where the policy will step, while the policy learns to leverage terrain information around those steps. With the proposed lightweight preprocessing, the policy reaches a given terrain difficulty in roughly a third of the training iterations required with the complete map. It outperforms policies that observe the complete map where footholds are sparse, including in narrow walled corridors, and on unseen terrain, and it matches an attention-based encoder trained at several times the cost. The policy transfers zero-shot to a Unitree G1 humanoid traversing various obstacles, stairs, gaps, and step-downs beyond the training distribution in both indoor and outdoor environments. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Space weather dependence of decameter-scale ionospheric irregularities spatial distribution
docs.text:
Space weather dependence of decameter-scale ionospheric irregularities spatial distribution Space weather dependence of decameter-scale ionospheric irregularities spatial distribution arXiv:2610.29630v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: This paper describes an approach to constructing nowcast and forecast predictive models for the occurrence of high-latitude decameter ionospheric irregularities based on SuperDARN and SECIRA radar data and space weather parameters. The method relies on self-learning pattern recognition in the dynamics of space weather parameters, that influence the irregularities formation. The proposed approach is a data-driven, multiscale method in which the spatial distribution of irregularities is approximated using a neural network of an original architecture, inspired by graph neural networks.
  The model was trained and tested using data from 11 radars during the period 2010-2025 (SuperDARN: CVW, ICE, ICW, INV, PGR, PYK, RKN, SAS, STO; SECIRA: EKB, MAGW). It is shown that the model achieves optimal performance when using geomagnetic coordinates MLT,MLAT. The optimal set of parameters for the best nowcast and forecast over studied set of parameters is a combination of geomagnetic and solar disturbance indices ($a_{p}$, $K_{p}$, $AE$, F10.7) from ground-based observations, and satellite-measured solar wind and interplanetary magnetic field parameters ($P_{sw}$, $E_{sw}$, $\widetilde{B_{z}}$, $T_{sw}$). Hourly mean values for all the parameters were used in the analysis. The results indicate that acceptable forecast quality is achieved with a lead time of up to 7-9 hours, with the highest quality reached for nowcast (zero lead time). It is shown that the parameters $\widetilde{B_{z}}$ and F10.7 are significant for nowcasting only and can be neglected for other lead times. It is shown that $AE$ and $T_{sw}$ are significant for mid-term forecast (\textgreater 2hours ahead) and can be neglected for short-term predictions.
  Statistical relationships between the maximum latitude of the equatorial boundary of the irregularities and space weather parameters are also discussed. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Recursive Code Evolution for Task-Oriented Semantic Communications
docs.text:
Recursive Code Evolution for Task-Oriented Semantic Communications Recursive Code Evolution for Task-Oriented Semantic Communications arXiv:2610.29641v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Semantic communication jointly optimizes inference accuracy, channel use, and computation, yet the underlying communication program is typically specified before training. This paper presents ComRSI (Communications-Oriented Recursive Self-Improvement), a framework for recursively evolving that program through large-language-model-assisted code edits. A fixed agent modifies the encoder, channel adapters, decoder, loss, and training policy; a protected evaluator screens candidates under prescribed budgets and resource constraints. Accepted code and textual feedback inform subsequent proposals, while candidate weights are trained from scratch. In the original ten-generation CIFAR-100 lineage, eight accepted revisions produce an attention-pooled code achieving 74.3% test accuracy over an Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) channel at 32 complex symbols per image, compared with 67.2% at 256 symbols for the initial design. The program also improves fading-channel accuracy and transfers to Tiny-ImageNet after retraining. A repeat study with ten searches per method compares ComRSI against non-recursive agents with and without textual history. Mean final search scores balancing accuracy, transmission rate, and computational cost are 0.7587, 0.7376, and 0.7089, respectively; the mean numbers of accepted revisions per search are 6.0, 5.0, and 2.1. The advantage over the memoryless agent is supported by a two-sided rank test, whereas the difference from the history-equipped agent remains statistically inconclusive at this sample size. Archived proposals show that pooling can yield a large improvement, while retained history supports subsequent refinement. These results support recursive program optimization within the evaluated setting and expose its remaining rate-robustness and compute-placement trade-offs. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Lineage-Aware Search Control for LLM-Based Evolutionary Factor Mining
docs.text:
Lineage-Aware Search Control for LLM-Based Evolutionary Factor Mining Lineage-Aware Search Control for LLM-Based Evolutionary Factor Mining arXiv:2610.29663v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Formulaic alpha factor mining searches for symbolic expressions that transform market data into predictive signals. Recent LLM-based evolutionary factor mining methods use large language models as semantic variation operators. Under the conventional LLM-EA paradigm, stochastic variation and fitness-based selection can leave the search weakly directed and concentrated around a narrow set of structurally similar factors. We argue that these limitations arise because current methods mainly organize search at the individual and population levels, leaving lineage-level control underused. A lineage connects successive factor variants through evolutionary descent. We propose LineageEvo, which uses lineage in two coupled forms of search control: (1) lineage-conditioned LLM variation, which distills Lineage-Scoped Search Experience into operator-specific priors and fuses them with global operator priors, providing persistent, lineage-relevant guidance for LLM generation; and (2) lineage-stratified search allocation, which balances factor quality against lineage concentration by distributing the search budget across lineages during evolutionary search. Together, these mechanisms make semantic variation more direction aware and prevent branches from dominating the evolution, thereby promoting the discovery of predictive and diverse factors. We evaluate LineageEvo on CSI 500 and S&P 500 in terms of factor predictiveness, portfolio performance, search efficiency, and lineage- and expression-level diversity. LineageEvo achieves the strongest predictive performance on both markets, while LSPS produces a more balanced lineage distribution and a structurally broader factor pool. The results support lineage as a useful intermediate unit for controlling LLM-based evolutionary factor search. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Lifting PCA in the Wasserstein Space
docs.text:
Lifting PCA in the Wasserstein Space Lifting PCA in the Wasserstein Space arXiv:2610.29679v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a fundamental tool for statistical dimension reduction, yet no canonical extension to distribution-valued data has emerged within the framework of optimal transport. While Wasserstein barycenters and Wasserstein least-squares regression provide canonical liftings of Euclidean averaging and linear regression in the Wasserstein space, an analogous principle for PCA has remained unexplored. In this paper, we introduce Lifted PCA, a canonical extension of Euclidean PCA to Wasserstein space, obtained through the framework of lifting functionals in the space of probability measures by convex extension. Starting from the classical variational formulations of PCA on the Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds, we derive two equivalent minimization problems over probability measures supported on these manifolds that correspond to Wasserstein barycenters with generalized costs. We establish an exact analogue of the equivalence between the Stiefel and Grassmann formulations of Euclidean PCA, preserving PCA's original variational structure under lifting. We further derive dual formulations and optimality conditions, and establish equivalences with multimarginal optimal transport and matching-for-teams problems. We also establish statistical consistency for empirical estimators and develop computational algorithms based on the Wasserstein barycenter formulation over the Stiefel manifold. Whereas Euclidean PCA summarizes vectors through projections onto an optimal low-dimensional linear subspace, Lifted PCA summarizes probability distributions through an optimal probability measure supported on multiple low-dimensional subspaces. Numerical experiments on distributional datasets illustrate the practical performance of the proposed methodology and its benefits for distributional data analysis. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking
docs.text:
TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking TraceForge: Distilling with Your Own Thinking arXiv:2610.29680v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Using an LLM to generate training data for another is among the most general ways to train one, and it remains common practice. Some frontier teams have closed that route for their own models: what comes back is an answer, or a short summary, without the detailed reasoning trace behind it. That is a little ironic: they were themselves built on distilling human knowledge, and distilling an open-source model is still entirely routine; the restriction applies to their own outputs alone. Recent work recovers the hidden reasoning by replaying encrypted blocks across models. It somehow works, but it breaks the providers' terms of service, so it is not something a product can be built on long-term.
  We built the alternative. We take the context and the teacher's answer as input, and generate the reasoning trace ourselves, in the style of the student's own model family. Training is two-stage, supervised and then adversarial: a generator learns to regenerate the family's own reasoning traces from their context and answer, and a critic learns how real a reasoning trace looks. Applied to a teacher's answer, the generator writes one in the family's style. An independent judge rates how likely traces are to be genuine on a scale from 0 to 1: ours average 0.68, real traces 0.66, and traces selected by the critic from four candidates 0.82. These are authenticity scores, not correctness rates.
  We test the idea on five benchmarks with everything else held fixed. On general tasks the five training corpora are about the same; on coding, the generated reasoning beats Fable 5's own thinking content. With the same 5,000 questions and the same teacher answers, HumanEval+ improves by 3.7 points and MBPP+ by 7.1 at the final checkpoint, and the MBPP+ lead holds at every checkpoint. We suspect that reasoning written in the student's family style is easier for it to learn from. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Rethinking Post-hoc Debiasing of Large Pretrained Models
docs.text:
Rethinking Post-hoc Debiasing of Large Pretrained Models Rethinking Post-hoc Debiasing of Large Pretrained Models arXiv:2610.29688v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Large pretrained models such as CLIP are widely used as frozen feature extractors. However, their embeddings inherit spurious correlations from training data, introducing bias into the features. A growing body of research has sought to address this issue through post hoc debiasing, leaving the backbone untouched. We discover that despite differing mechanisms, these methods require the bias feature to be identified and expressed in text. This dependency is not innocuous. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate that this requirement incurs an unforeseen penalty in certain scenarios. For example, on the UrbanCars benchmark, having two co-occurring bias attributes, the recent methods underperform a vanilla classifier on biased frozenbackbone features, and even providing ground-truth bias identities does not close the gap. We show that the pattern that such methods seek is readily observable in the frozen geometry. Specifically, cross-class training pairs placed closest together by the frozen encoder almost always share a spurious attribute, regardless of the bias type, without requiring access to the bias labels. Based on this, we propose a novel approach to identify such pairs and learn a single linear map that transforms the features to perform post-hoc debiasing. The proposed approach achieves competitive performance across all datasets without access to bias attribute annotations or any LLMs. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Post-hoc Epistemic Uncertainty for Vision-Language-Action Policies
docs.text:
Post-hoc Epistemic Uncertainty for Vision-Language-Action Policies Post-hoc Epistemic Uncertainty for Vision-Language-Action Policies arXiv:2610.29730v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies need to recognize gaps in their training knowledge to request useful demonstrations or assistance in new situations, especially when failures are costly. Disagreement within an ensemble of independently trained policies can guide these decisions, but requires training and running multiple policies. We propose post-hoc kernel-variance heads that estimate epistemic uncertainty from the embeddings of a single policy. Each head computes the conditional variance of a Gaussian process conditioned on embeddings from the training demonstrations. Fitting requires no regression targets or gradient updates and leaves the policy unchanged. In experiments with SmolVLA on LIBERO-10, the kernel variance heads perform competitively with two-policy ensemble scores in task-level correlation with task success, in demonstration acquisition during active learning, and in referral to a stronger supervisor policy as a proxy for human assistance. For SmolVLA, the head on the vision-language backbone reduces uncertainty-scoring time by up to approximately a factor of 50 compared with ensemble scores, while also substantially reducing setup costs. We also show that the established evaluation protocol on LIBERO-10 primarily rewards recognition of coverage differences between tasks, while execution variability weakens assessment of within-task rankings. Thus, controlled perturbations provide a complementary evaluation: modality-specific heads identify unfamiliar camera, instruction, or state inputs, while fused heads can detect unfamiliar combinations of individually familiar inputs. With a supervisor proxy trained on the evaluated perturbation families, the decoder head improves within-task referral over ensemble disagreement. These findings show that useful uncertainty estimates for adaptive robot learning can be obtained from a single policy. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Where Do LLMs Learn to Recommend AI?
docs.text:
Where Do LLMs Learn to Recommend AI? Where Do LLMs Learn to Recommend AI? arXiv:2610.29785v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Asked what to study, which career to pursue, or what product to build, large language models (LLMs) often recommend AI-related options. We ask where this tendency comes from by comparing models before and after fine-tuning and by varying how questions are asked. First, pretrained models already include explicit AI/ML terms in the recommendations of 27% of their responses, and their released instruction-tuned versions do so in 59%. Second, fine-tuning models ourselves shows that this rise is not inevitable: general instruction tuning leaves the rate unchanged, but removing the 7% of instruction examples that concern AI cuts it by 14 percentage points, below the level of the pretrained models it starts from. Data rewarding helpfulness raise it by 9 points, while data ranked by the preferences of diverse simulated users lower it by 9. Finally, with models held fixed, asking for the "best" option or for what to do "right now" raises the rate by 8 and 18 points, whereas telling the model it is an AI advisor adds 4. Overall, the tendency starts in pretraining, and what models learn afterward, together with how a question is phrased, decides how strongly it appears. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents
docs.text:
Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents arXiv:2610.29812v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Literature-searching language agents are becoming a standard component of scientific assistants for the life sciences, yet there is little controlled evidence on which parts of their harness matter. We run a controlled ablation on biomedical claim verification (SciFact) with the live PubMed API as the only tool. Holding the backbone and output format fixed, we compare four harnesses: closed-book answering, single-shot retrieval using the claim as the query, a ReAct-style agent that writes its own PubMed queries, and an oracle given the gold abstracts, each with two efficient frontier backbones. Naive single-shot retrieval finds the gold paper for only 6% of claims and turns overconfident errors into abstentions without improving accuracy. Letting the model formulate its own queries triples gold recall and yields the best verdicts (62% accuracy vs. 49-59% for the other realistic harnesses), although these differences are not significant at our sample size and agents use fewer than half of their search budget. With gold abstracts, the same models reach 79-86% accuracy, a significant 17-24 point gap showing that retrieval, not reasoning, is the main bottleneck. Finally, a citation audit shows that closed-book models cite PubMed IDs that almost always exist (327/335) but are almost never relevant: a cross-family LLM judge rates only 3 of 327 existing citations as relevant to the claim, versus 67% for citations produced by the search agent. Existence checks are therefore insufficient safeguards for scientific agents. We release code, prompts, and all cached tool calls at https://github.com/saqlain2204/real-pmids-wrong-papers. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: NeuroCodec: EEG-Guided Latent-Domain Generative Model for High-Fidelity Target Speaker Extraction
docs.text:
NeuroCodec: EEG-Guided Latent-Domain Generative Model for High-Fidelity Target Speaker Extraction NeuroCodec: EEG-Guided Latent-Domain Generative Model for High-Fidelity Target Speaker Extraction arXiv:2610.29815v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Driven by recent advancements in hearing assistive devices, target speaker extraction (TSE) in multi-talker environments has drawn significant attention. To address this, hearing technologies identify attention using neural signals recorded via electroencephalography (EEG) to guide TSE, enabling neuro-steered auditory attention decoding. However, most existing techniques rely on time-frequency masking, which suffers from low fidelity in spectro-temporally overlapping regions and is often restricted to narrowband audio. In contrast, we introduce NeuroCodec, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first generative EEG-guided TSE framework operating in the latent space of a neural audio codec. Specifically, NeuroCodec models spatial EEG dependencies via graph convolutions and fuses cross-modal EEG and speech representations through attention mechanisms and Mamba-based temporal modeling. We further introduce a six-phase training curriculum that progressively incorporates latent reconstruction, multi-scale spectral, and adversarial objectives to ensure stable, high-fidelity speech generation. Experiments on the public Cocktail Party and KUL datasets show NeuroCodec outperforms baselines, across several perceptual metrics. A listening experiment with 20 participants validated that NeuroCodec offers greater perceptual accuracy, achieving a mean score of 82.24 compared with 49.63 for M3ANet. Additionally, the proposed method is seen to enable 44.1 kHz reconstruction with spectral content extending up to 20 kHz, further supporting the perceptual results. Finally, we extend NeuroCodec with a causal streaming formulation suited for real-time processing, providing a basis for hearing assistive devices. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: RangeNav: Task-Aligned LiDAR Range-Image Pretraining for Robot Navigation
docs.text:
RangeNav: Task-Aligned LiDAR Range-Image Pretraining for Robot Navigation RangeNav: Task-Aligned LiDAR Range-Image Pretraining for Robot Navigation arXiv:2610.29845v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Autonomous mobile robots operating in dense crowds and cluttered sites require $360^\circ$ perception to react to surrounding hazards. While panoramic LiDAR offers full-surround coverage, learning representations within reinforcement learning (RL) is sample-inefficient under sparse rewards, and existing 3D pretrained point-cloud encoders are too memory-heavy for massively parallel RL simulation. We present RangeNav, a compact (183k parameters) LiDAR range-image encoder pretrained entirely on synthetic data. RangeNav uses anisotropic convolutions and circular padding to handle the extreme aspect ratio and azimuthal seam of range images. We pretrain the network using a navigation-aligned objective combining range reconstruction, semantic segmentation, and bird's-eye-view (BEV) prediction, then freeze it for policy learning. In simulation, adding semantic and BEV supervision increases success rates over a reconstruction-only baseline by an average of 32.03 and 23.73 percentage points (pp) in procedurally generated training and out-of-distribution realistic test environments, respectively. Zero-shot real-world deployments on a Unitree B2-W quadruped demonstrate robust navigation through dense crowds, low-light settings, and construction zones where limited-field-of-view depth policies struggle. Code and models will be open-sourced. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Silent Alignment in Two-Layer Linear Networks: A High-Dimensional Perspective
docs.text:
Silent Alignment in Two-Layer Linear Networks: A High-Dimensional Perspective Silent Alignment in Two-Layer Linear Networks: A High-Dimensional Perspective arXiv:2610.29864v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We study gradient flow in a two-layer linear network in the high-dimensional regime where the input, inner and output dimensions diverge proportionally. Under whitened inputs and isotropic imbalance, we combine a closed-form solution of the dynamics with prior random matrix theory results to derive a high-dimensional limit for the dynamics. Our method yields exact asymptotic spectral distributions for the weight matrices at all times and characterizes the evolution of the learned subspace. In the small-initialization limit, we identify a silent alignment phenomenon: the singular directions of the network align on an order-one timescale, while the singular values and empirical loss remain at their initial values. Visible learning occurs later, on a logarithmic timescale, as singular values progressively escape zero and the loss decreases. This phase is characterized by a saddle-to-saddle dynamics, which becomes a continuous process of spectral learning in the high-dimensional limit. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
docs.text:
Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks Tractable Inference with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks arXiv:2610.29909v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Machine-learning surrogates in computational science often require not only accurate predictions but also expectations, variances, conserved integrals, and normalization constants. Conventional neural networks, including Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs), generally evaluate these quantities through Monte Carlo sampling or multidimensional quadrature, making repeated inference costly, particularly in high dimensions. We introduce KANs with Tractable Operators for Uncertainty and Constraints (TOUCKANs), whose finite-degree polynomial outer functions yield a decomposable sum--product representation. Under factorizing input measures, expectations and higher moments then reduce algebraically to deterministic recursions over one-dimensional leaf integrals. Independent and shared inner-block variants form a parameter-efficiency hierarchy, and a universal-approximation proof for its most restricted member extends to the complete class. The same deterministic operators allow conserved integrals and normalization to be imposed throughout training. Across uniform and Gaussian benchmarks through 50 dimensions, deterministic mean and variance errors remained below the median fixed-budget Monte Carlo errors in every case. TOUCKANs also conserved Cahn--Hilliard mass to machine precision and imposed normalization and orthogonality through deterministic moments, enabling joint computation of the lowest four Schr\"odinger eigenpairs in two, three, and five dimensions. TOUCKANs therefore connect KAN approximation with tractable probabilistic circuits, making statistical operators and integral constraints directly available within an expressive neural surrogate. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Unintended Side Effects of Value Training in LLMs
docs.text:
Unintended Side Effects of Value Training in LLMs Unintended Side Effects of Value Training in LLMs arXiv:2610.29922v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: As LLMs are increasingly deployed in value-sensitive contexts, aligning them with human values has emerged as a post-training objective in NLP, aimed at instilling additional values and guiding model behaviour. However, current evaluations remain narrow. Because values are interconnected, it is unclear how fine-tuning for specific values alters unrelated capabilities and behaviours. In this work, we adapt four instruction-tuned LLMs across individual Hofstede's value dimensions and evaluate them on both cross-value transfer and broader behaviours. We find that value-specific training produces unintended side effects on untrained values, risk preferences, social cognition, and safety traits. Consequently, we suggest that value alignment after post-training should incorporate broader behavioral evaluations, and we highlight the need to investigate where additional value training might best fit into the pipeline. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Mastering Model Fit: Applications of the InterModel Vigorish for Interpretable Machine Learning
docs.text:
Mastering Model Fit: Applications of the InterModel Vigorish for Interpretable Machine Learning Mastering Model Fit: Applications of the InterModel Vigorish for Interpretable Machine Learning arXiv:2610.29960v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Accuracy alone gives little information about which features or model components improve probabilistic fit, which outcomes benefit, or how fit changes during training. We introduce the InterModel Vigorish (IMV) into the Machine Intelligence space in order to express differences in fit as an expected betting advantage over a reference model. SHAP-IMV attributes gains to features through Shapley-weighted subset comparisons, Multi-IMV evaluates one-vs-rest and pairwise class discrimination, and Ablate-IMV assesses architectural components and feature groups by ablation. We evaluate these applications over ten random seeds using tabular data, images, sensor sequences, and graphs. Feature rankings vary across estimators. High one-vs-rest accuracy can accompany negligible improvement over a null, while ablation can preserve or improve fit under a fixed training budget. On six graph-classification benchmarks, we time-profile IMV over 200 training epochs, reporting seed means and ranges. The open-source imvpy library and accompanying notebooks provide code to replicate our work and to use the IMV more widely. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: The Price of Current-Effect Inference in Nonstationary Multi-Armed Bandits
docs.text:
The Price of Current-Effect Inference in Nonstationary Multi-Armed Bandits The Price of Current-Effect Inference in Nonstationary Multi-Armed Bandits arXiv:2610.29982v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Adaptive experiments use bandit algorithms to favor interventions with higher expected rewards. However, decision-makers also require reliable inference on current treatment effects: differences between intervention and reference-arm mean rewards at the present time, rather than historical averages. These objectives conflict: reward maximization favors better interventions, whereas current-effect inference requires continued exploration of potentially suboptimal interventions as outcomes change over time. We characterize this tradeoff for $K$-arm bandits with H\"older-smooth mean rewards of exponent $\beta\in(0,1]$ and constant $L$. Requiring high-probability simultaneous coverage of all current effects by confidence intervals of width at most $w$, we establish matching minimax bounds, up to logarithmic factors, on expected dynamic regret. Over horizon $T$, our algorithm TRACE (Tracking Rewards and Current Effects) achieves regret of order $\widetilde{O}_{\beta}\left(\sqrt{KT}+K^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}L^{1/(2\beta+1)}T^{(\beta+1)/(2\beta+1)}+Kw^{-2}(1+L^{1/\beta}w^{-1/\beta})\right)$, where the notation hides logarithms and constants depending only on $\beta$. This regret--precision tradeoff separates reward-learning regret from the cost of refreshing current-effect estimates, which remains unavoidable even when one arm is uniformly optimal. An empirical-Bernstein e-process extension adapts exploration to realized prediction errors while preserving worst-case guarantees. When within-block drift is negligible relative to sampling error, all observations, including reward-learning observations, can be reused for asymptotically normal pointwise inference and stronger local stationarity yields local asymptotic efficiency. Finally, we show that regret constraints can prevent honest adaptation to unknown smoothness and support our theory with extensive numerical experiments. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: TIDE: Tree-Induced Fine-Grained Diagnostic Evaluation from Model Behaviors
docs.text:
TIDE: Tree-Induced Fine-Grained Diagnostic Evaluation from Model Behaviors TIDE: Tree-Induced Fine-Grained Diagnostic Evaluation from Model Behaviors arXiv:2610.29985v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Benchmark performance is the dominant standard for comparing large language models (LLMs), typically summarized by a single aggregate score, such as accuracy, pass rate, or rubric score. This aggregate score provides limited information about a model's underlying capabilities, yet understanding these capabilities is crucial for model development and evaluation. To this end, we propose Tree-Induced Diagnostic Evaluation (TIDE), which recasts diagnostic evaluation as behavior-driven decision-tree induction to perform fine-grained capability diagnosis. TIDE recursively builds a hierarchical capability tree from benchmark samples and model scores: at each node, an LLM judge proposes candidate splits and performs sample-to-group classification, and behavior-based information gain selects among them. We apply TIDE to five models across four benchmarks to demonstrate its effectiveness, and find fine-grained capability contrasts invisible at the aggregate level: Claude Opus 4.6 achieves 100% on microeconomic market reasoning where GPT-5.4 scores 83.3%, but trails GPT-5.4 on contract law reasoning with 77.8% versus 88.9%. We hope TIDE can be extended to past and future benchmarks so that the rich behavioral signal in evaluation results is fully leveraged for understanding model capabilities. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Code Comprehensor: Hierarchical Documentation and Cross-Modal Retrieval for Large Repositories
docs.text:
Code Comprehensor: Hierarchical Documentation and Cross-Modal Retrieval for Large Repositories Code Comprehensor: Hierarchical Documentation and Cross-Modal Retrieval for Large Repositories arXiv:2610.30016v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Understanding large, complex, and rapidly evolving code bases remains a core challenge for software engineering at scale, hindering onboarding, maintenance, refactoring, and impact analysis. Providing this information to a Large-Language Model (LLM) is another hurdle, as the LLM must understand not only the required code method but also its associated methods in the grand scheme of the repository. We propose Code Comprehensor, a hybrid retrieval-reasoning framework combining (i) a code dependency callgraph, (ii) CodeScribe, which uses code-aware LLMs to generate hierarchical documentation across repository call graphs, and (iii) CodeContrast, a CLIP-style dual-encoder model trained on CodeScribe output to learn aligned text-code embeddings. CodeContrast enables fast, semantically precise retrieval of relevant code-context neighborhoods, which serve as grounded evidence for an MCP-based LLM orchestrator answering domain-specific queries. Evaluation on OpenCV and a proprietary 5M-LOC repository shows that CodeScribe-derived supervision significantly improves cross-modal retrieval in text-to-code accuracy over baseline approaches. Richer textual supervision (hierarchical documentation, parent/sibling context, and LLM-generated synthetic questions) consistently enhances performance across both repositories. LLM-as-a-judge evaluation using the popular RAGAS of the Code Comprehensor output yields above 90% faithfulness scores. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: HGM-Dual: Lineage-Aware Guided Agent Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Planning
docs.text:
HGM-Dual: Lineage-Aware Guided Agent Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Planning HGM-Dual: Lineage-Aware Guided Agent Harness Optimization for Long-Horizon Planning arXiv:2610.30042v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Harness optimization, which improves an agent's prompts, tools, and workflows, is an increasingly effective way to enhance agents built on frozen or closed-source LLMs. Leading approaches such as the Darwin--Godel Machine and the Huxley--Godel Machine (HGM) rely on recursive self-improvement and were developed mainly for coding, where the competence needed to improve the agent coincides with the competence being improved. Planning tasks, in which an agent must produce a sequence of tool calls that jointly satisfies interacting constraints, break this alignment. There, open-ended self-modification repeatedly explores ineffective changes and consumes substantial evaluation budgets. We introduce HGM-Dual, a diagnostic-guided framework for budget-efficient harness evolution for planning agents. First, HGM-Dual represents agent evolution as lineage-aware context. This context records what each ancestor changed, which behaviors improved or regressed, and which modifications were ineffective, giving the editor explicit edit-outcome attribution instead of an unstructured archive of past agents. Second, HGM-Dual introduces error-conditioned dual-path child generation. For each selected parent, it generates a general child that preserves open-ended exploration and specialized children that target the harness components most likely responsible for the parent's highest-ranked constraint violations. HGM-Dual outperforms the strongest baseline by up to 14.45% relative improvement in case accuracy while matching HGM variants' final performance with 2x-4x fewer evaluation budget. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models
docs.text:
Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models Looped Uniform Diffusion Language Models arXiv:2610.30066v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Uniform diffusion language models (UDLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising sequences of ordinary vocabulary tokens, any of which may be corrupted and subsequently revised. During training, UDLMs must denoise from a context that may itself be unreliable, whereas masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) always condition on a clean context. This challenging training objective makes UDLMs more FLOP-intensive to train than MDLMs, but it yields stronger downstream reasoning performance. Recently, selective looping, which recursively applies a few early Transformer layers within each denoising step, has been shown to improve training efficiency in MDLMs under an iso-FLOP budget. We investigate looping in UDLMs while keeping the training objective and sampler unchanged. We find that looping significantly improves training efficiency: looped UDLMs reach the validation NLL of a non-looped UDLM trained on about 0.5 trillion tokens with up to 2.8x fewer training FLOPs on OpenWebText and 3.3x fewer on FineWeb-Edu. We also find that, at a matched NFE budget, looped UDLMs reach up to 9.8% lower generation perplexity than the non-looped UDLM, with most gains achieved at moderate loop counts. Finally, we study different loop-count distributions and find that sampling smaller loop counts more frequently during training improves inference efficiency: on downstream tasks, this strategy uses 12% fewer loops than uniform loop-count sampling without degrading accuracy. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift
docs.text:
VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift VX-One: Typed, Calibrated Decision Heads for Real-Time Perimeter Triage - An empirical study of unknown-attack honesty, cascade gray zones, and calibration under drift arXiv:2610.30090v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Perimeter triage faces a latency/semantics trade-off: signature engines are fast and format-safe but blind to unseen attacks, while generative models are semantic but slow and produce unparseable output. In late 2026 a class of commercial System One decision models (TypeSafe Jev; Microsoft-Decision-1) began selling typed decision primitives - binary gates, closed-set choices, ordinal scores - as product APIs, with no academic treatment. We present VX-One: a small multi-head network (100K-10M parameters) whose outputs are these primitives - a calibrated gate, a choice over a closed candidate set that always includes an explicit unknown option, and an ordinal score, trained multi-task, temperature-calibrated per head (~0.7-1.7 ms p50 on CPU). We evaluate it on UNSW-NB15, CIC-IDS2017, EMBER2024 against calibrated XGBoost, Random-Forest, MLP, Kitsune, and measure a two-phase cascade (Suricata with 52,674 Emerging-Threats rules -> VX-One) over five days of CIC-IDS2017. Findings: (i) VX-One wins detection (AUROC/FPR@95%TPR) on UNSW-NB15 and under temporal drift on CIC-IDS2017 (0.711 vs 0.637), but XGBoost wins multi-class attribution on all three benchmarks; (ii) leave-one-family-out gate detects never-seen families on 9/9 UNSW folds yet drops below chance on CIC recon family, and abstention threshold transfers poorly across benchmarks; (iii) on payload-less reconstructions signature engines resolve ~0.1% of flows - gray zone ~99.9% of traffic, recovered by Phase 2 (combined recall >=0.978); (iv) calibration collapses under temporal drift (ECE 0.04->0.40) for every method while ranking partially survives. We provide a measured account of where typed calibrated decisions help perimeter triage, and where they fail. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
docs.text:
Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration arXiv:2610.30105v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Sequential decision-making under partial observability is difficult because agents must explore to infer hidden, task-relevant information before acting effectively. Learning such information-gathering behaviors tabula rasa via online reinforcement learning is sample-inefficient, whereas offline imitation averages expert actions across hidden states and fails to learn exploration. In this work, we propose ASTEROID, a simple and effective student--teacher supervised learning framework that can learn test-time exploration. Although a privileged expert never needs to explore, we demonstrate that a history-conditioned student can learn to do so when trained with on-policy contexts: the student first collects on-policy context under partial observability, and the privileged expert provides action labels conditioned on that context. By distilling expert actions directly conditioned on the student's on-policy history, the student learns to systematically resolve partial observability, i.e., search while uncertain and exploit once the hidden state is revealed. This enables efficient test-time exploration (similar to Bayesian posterior sampling) without incurring the impractical training-data costs of reinforcement learning. Across a diverse range of eleven different environments, including discrete exploration benchmarks, robotic manipulation, navigation, and Procgen environments, ASTEROID achieves ~2x higher returns under fixed exploration budgets, uses ~100x fewer interactions than RL baselines, and outperforms frontier models at exploration. Finally, our method transfers policies trained in simulation to vision-denied real-world robot manipulation, exhibiting efficient exploration and increasing success by +40% over standard distillation. Overall, it provides a simple yet surprisingly effective framework to learn efficient test-time exploration. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance
docs.text:
Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance Minimax Optimality of the NPMLE for Gaussian Mixtures in Hellinger Distance arXiv:2610.30109v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We analyze the problem of estimating univariate Gaussian mixture densities using the nonparametric maximum likelihood estimator (NPMLE) based on $n$ independent and identically distributed samples. We show that the unconstrained NPMLE achieves the minimax optimal rate $\log(n)/n$ in squared Hellinger distance, when the true mixing measure is sub-Gaussian. In addition, we show that when the true mixing measure has compact support, the NMPLE constrained to a compact interval also achieves the minimax optimal rate, which is slightly faster and of order $\log(n)/(n \log \log n)$. Our proof consists of sharply characterizing the local Hellinger bracketing entropy of the class of finite Gaussian mixtures. One of our key technical innovations is to sharply bound the $L^2$ bracketing entropy of balls of bounded-degree polynomials, which may be of independent interest. As an application, we establish the regret-optimality of $g$-modeling procedures based on the NPMLE in the Gaussian Empirical Bayes problem with bounded priors. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions
docs.text:
A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions arXiv:2610.30122v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We give an algorithm for computing an $\eps$-approximate fixed point of any $d$-dimensional nonexpansion with respect to the $\ell_\infty$ norm in time $\log(1/\eps)^{O(\log^2 d)}$. At its core, our method uses a boosting argument to geometrically shrink a search region. Among other consequences, our algorithm implies that simple stochastic games can be solved in quasipolynomial time. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
docs.text:
Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation Think Harder Where It Matters: Item-Level Adaptive Recursion for Sequential Recommendation arXiv:2610.30128v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Existing sequential recommenders usually allocate a fixed computational budget to every item in a user's interaction history, regardless of the item's contribution to the final prediction. We challenge this de facto design with two diagnostic findings. (1) Non-uniform computational need: items within the same sequence vary drastically in how much computation they require. Most converge after shallow processing while a critical minority only stabilizes at full depth. (2) Suboptimality of fixed allocation: given oracle access to the target item, a non-uniform depth assignment consistently outranks the fixed one, indicating that existing uniform computation both wastes capacity on already-converged items and sacrifices overall recommendation quality. These observations motivate a shift from fixed-depth computation to item-level adaptive reasoning. To this end, we propose LoopRec. LoopRec recursively applies a single weight-shared block and introduces a lightweight gate at each recursion boundary that makes a binary exit-or-continue decision for every item independently. Items whose representations have sufficiently matured exit early, while those requiring deeper reasoning continue to subsequent recursions. This design converts the fixed global depth into a learned, per-item property without auxiliary depth labels, and is readily adaptable to diverse backbone architectures. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks with four backbone families demonstrate that LoopRec consistently outperforms matched fixed-depth counterparts. Further analysis reveals that LoopRec's learned allocation exhibits interpretable patterns aligned with our post-hoc oracle analysis: lower-frequency items and more recent interactions naturally receive deeper computation. Our code is available at https://github.com/Elpmis117/LoopRec. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
docs.text:
LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data arXiv:2610.30132v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is an effective way to strengthen the long-context reasoning of large language models (LLMs), but it needs training data that are long, diverse, challenging, and verifiable. Human annotation of such data is expensive, naturally occurring data are too scarce to sustain RL, and existing synthesis methods depend on external corpora or stronger teacher models, which become harder to obtain as the trained models get stronger. Recently, RL from zero data, in which a model learns from tasks it proposes itself, has achieved excellent performance, but existing methods target short-context tasks. Therefore, we propose $\textbf{LongZero}$, a method that lets an LLM improve its own long-context reasoning without any external data. Instead of writing questions and answers over existing documents, LongZero first has the model synthesize the question and answer with its supporting evidence in a compact structured form, and only then separately expands the evidence into a long multi-document context. LongZero combines these self-written multi-hop reasoning tasks with self-written multi-round retrieval tasks and trains the model with GRPO. We evaluate LongZero on two LLMs across five long-context reasoning benchmarks and compare it with RL on data synthesized from external corpora. Experimental results show that LongZero can generalize to real tasks, and outperforms both baselines, suggesting a viable and promising path to improving long-context reasoning of LLMs. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: The Limits of Post-Selection Generalization
docs.text:
The Limits of Post-Selection Generalization The Limits of Post-Selection Generalization arXiv:1806.06100v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: While statistics and machine learning offer numerous methods for ensuring generalization, these methods often fail in the presence of adaptivity---the common practice in which the choice of analysis depends on previous interactions with the same dataset. A recent line of work has introduced powerful, general purpose algorithms that ensure post hoc generalization (also called robust or post-selection generalization), which says that, given the output of the algorithm, it is hard to find any statistic for which the data differs significantly from the population it came from.
  In this work we show several limitations on the power of algorithms satisfying post hoc generalization. First, we show a tight lower bound on the error of any algorithm that satisfies post hoc generalization and answers adaptively chosen statistical queries, showing a strong barrier to progress in post selection data analysis. Second, we show that post hoc generalization is not closed under composition, despite many examples of such algorithms exhibiting strong composition properties. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Multi-Label Sentiment Analysis on 100 Languages with Dynamic Weighting for Label Imbalance
docs.text:
Multi-Label Sentiment Analysis on 100 Languages with Dynamic Weighting for Label Imbalance Multi-Label Sentiment Analysis on 100 Languages with Dynamic Weighting for Label Imbalance arXiv:2008.11573v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We investigate cross-lingual sentiment analysis, which has attracted significant attention due to its applications in various areas including market research, politics and social sciences. In particular, we introduce a sentiment analysis framework in multi-label setting as it obeys Plutchik's wheel of emotions. We introduce a novel dynamic weighting method that balances the contribution from each class during training, unlike previous static weighting methods that assign non-changing weights based on their class frequency. Moreover, we adapt the focal loss that favors harder instances from single-label object recognition literature to our multi-label setting. Furthermore, we derive a method to choose optimal class-specific thresholds that maximize the macro-f1 score in linear time complexity. Through an extensive set of experiments, we show that our method obtains the state-of-the-art performance in 7 of 9 metrics in 3 different languages using a single model compared to the common baselines and the best-performing methods in the SemEval competition. We publicly share our code for our model, which can perform sentiment analysis in 100 languages, to facilitate further research. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Quantifying Symptom Causality in Clinical Decision Making: An Exploration Using CausaLM
docs.text:
Quantifying Symptom Causality in Clinical Decision Making: An Exploration Using CausaLM Quantifying Symptom Causality in Clinical Decision Making: An Exploration Using CausaLM arXiv:2503.19394v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Current machine learning approaches to medical diagnosis often rely on correlational patterns between symptoms and diseases, risking misdiagnoses when symptoms are ambiguous or common across multiple conditions. In this work, we move beyond correlation to investigate the causal influence of key symptoms-specifically "chest pain" on diagnostic predictions. Leveraging the CausaLM framework, we generate counterfactual text representations in which target concepts are effectively "forgotten" enabling a principled estimation of the causal effect of that concept on a model's predicted disease distribution. By employing Textual Representation-based Average Treatment Effect (TReATE), we quantify how the presence or absence of a symptom shapes the model's diagnostic outcomes, and contrast these findings against correlation-based baselines such as CONEXP. Our results offer deeper insight into the decision-making behavior of clinical NLP models and have the potential to inform more trustworthy, interpretable, and causally-grounded decision support tools in medical practice. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Remote Rowhammer Attack using Adversarial Observations on Federated Learning Clients
docs.text:
Remote Rowhammer Attack using Adversarial Observations on Federated Learning Clients Remote Rowhammer Attack using Adversarial Observations on Federated Learning Clients arXiv:2505.06335v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has the potential for simultaneous global learning amongst a large number of parallel agents, enabling emerging AI systems to be trained across demographically diverse data. Central to this being efficient is the ability for FL to perform sparse gradient updates and remote direct memory access at the central server. Most of the research in FL security focuses on protecting data privacy at the edge client or in the communication channels between the client and server. Client-facing attacks on the server are less well investigated as the assumption is that a large collective of clients offer resilience. Here, for the first time, we show that by attacking clients that lead to repetitive clustered memory updates in the server, we can remote initiate a rowhammer attack to corrupt the server memory with induced bit-flips. A reinforcement learning (RL) attacker without backdoor access to the server can learn how to maximize server repetitive clustered memory updates by manipulating the clients' sensor observation. We demonstrate the feasibility of our attack using FL systems with sparse updates, tasked for automatic speech recognition (ASR) as well as CIFAR10 classification, our adversarial attacking agent can achieve around 70% repeated update rate (RUR) in the targeted server model, effectively inducing bit flips on server DRAM. The security implications are that such adversarial observations can cause disruptions to learning or may inadvertently cause elevated privilege, which could pave the way for further research on practical mitigation strategies in FL and hardware design. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Understanding and Mitigating Under-Confidence in GNNs from the Final Layer
docs.text:
Understanding and Mitigating Under-Confidence in GNNs from the Final Layer Understanding and Mitigating Under-Confidence in GNNs from the Final Layer arXiv:2505.11335v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have demonstrated remarkable effectiveness on graph-based tasks. However, their predictive confidence is often miscalibrated, typically exhibiting under-confidence, which harms the reliability of their decisions. Existing calibration methods for GNNs normally introduce additional calibration components, which fail to capture the intrinsic relationship between the model and the prediction confidence, resulting in limited theoretical guarantees and increased computational overhead. To address this issue, we propose a simple yet efficient graph calibration method. We establish a unified theoretical framework revealing that model confidence is jointly governed by class-centroid-level and node-level calibration at the final layer. Based on this insight, we theoretically show that reducing the weight decay of the final-layer parameters alleviates GNN under-confidence by acting on the class-centroid level, while node-level calibration acts as a finer-grained complement to class-centroid-level calibration, which encourages each test node to be closer to its predicted class prototype in the final-layer representations. Extensive experiments validate the superiority of our method. The code is released at https://github.com/huangJC0429/SCAR. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Quality-Diversity Red-Teaming: Automated Generation of High-Quality and Diverse Attackers for Large Language Models
docs.text:
Quality-Diversity Red-Teaming: Automated Generation of High-Quality and Diverse Attackers for Large Language Models Quality-Diversity Red-Teaming: Automated Generation of High-Quality and Diverse Attackers for Large Language Models arXiv:2506.07121v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Ensuring the safety and robustness of large language models (LLMs) is a fundamental challenge and a critical prerequisite for the responsible deployment of artificial intelligence. Red-teaming, a systematic framework to identify adversarial prompts that elicit harmful responses from target LLMs, has emerged as a crucial safety evaluation paradigm. Within this framework, the diversity of adversarial prompts is critical for a comprehensive safety assessment. However, previous red-teaming approaches often pursue diversity through simplistic metrics such as word frequency or sentence embedding similarity, which may not capture meaningful variation in attack strategies. In addition, the common practice of training a single attacker model restricts coverage across all potential attack styles and risk categories. This paper introduces Quality-Diversity Red-Teaming (QDRT), a new framework designed to address these limitations. QDRT achieves goal-driven diversity through behavior-conditioned training and implements a behavioral replay buffer in an open-ended manner. In addition, it trains multiple specialized attackers capable of generating high-quality attacks across diverse styles and risk categories. Our empirical evaluation demonstrates that QDRT generates attacks that are both more diverse and more effective against a wide range of target LLMs, including open-source models \texttt{GPT-2}, \texttt{Llama-3}, \texttt{Gemma-2}, \texttt{Qwen2.5}, and commercial models \texttt{GPT-4.1} and \texttt{GPT-5-Chat}. This work advances the field of LLM safety by providing a systematic and effective approach to automated red-teaming, ultimately supporting the responsible deployment of LLMs. Our code is available at https://github.com/lamda-bbo/QDRT. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: In-Context Bias Propagation in LLM-Based Tabular Data Generation
docs.text:
In-Context Bias Propagation in LLM-Based Tabular Data Generation In-Context Bias Propagation in LLM-Based Tabular Data Generation arXiv:2506.09630v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used for synthetic tabular data generation through in-context learning (ICL), offering a practical solution for data augmentation in data scarce scenarios. While prior work has shown the potential of LLMs to improve downstream task performance through augmenting underrepresented groups, these benefits often assume access to a subset of unbiased in-context examples, representative of the real dataset. In real-world settings, however, data is frequently noisy and demographically skewed. In this paper, we systematically study how statistical biases within in-context examples propagate to synthetic tabular data, showing that even mild in-context biases lead to global statistical distortions. We further introduce an adversarial scenario where a malicious contributor can inject bias into the synthetic dataset via a subset of in-context examples, ultimately compromising the fairness of downstream classifiers for a targeted and protected subgroup. Finally, we evaluate prompt-side mitigation strategies based on preprocessing in-context examples and instruction-based defenses, demonstrating that while such techniques can attenuate disparity, the inherent sensitivity of LLMs to adversarial prompts remains a persistent challenge. Our findings highlight a critical new vulnerability in LLM-based data generation pipelines within sensitive domains. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of Global Radiation from Sparse Sensor Sequences
docs.text:
Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of Global Radiation from Sparse Sensor Sequences Spatiotemporal Reconstruction of Global Radiation from Sparse Sensor Sequences arXiv:2506.12045v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Much of the physical world is inaccessible to direct measurement and can be reached only through the sparse traces it leaves in other observable variables. Here we introduce the Temporal Radiation Operator Network (TRON), a spatiotemporal neural operator that learns proxy-to-field mappings, reconstructing otherwise unobserved physical fields from sparse, indirect sensor histories. For cosmic-radiation mapping, TRON reconstructs sea-level effective dose at 65,341 locations from histories of 12 neutron monitors, achieving 0.096\% mean relative $L_2$ error against EXPACS-generated reference fields in a chronologically held-out year; batched GPU inference evaluates a global field in approximately $\sim$1~ms, compared with $\sim$57.6~s for EXPACS on one CPU thread. On measured weather networks, TRON reconstructs temperature at held-out stations from thermometer or barometer histories, outperforming interpolation, calendar-based and hypsometric baselines. These results establish proxy-to-field reconstruction as a general route to recovering spatially distributed physical information beyond the direct reach of sparse sensor networks. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Energy-Based Transfer for Reinforcement Learning
docs.text:
Energy-Based Transfer for Reinforcement Learning Energy-Based Transfer for Reinforcement Learning arXiv:2506.16590v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning remains sample inefficient, particularly when agents must adapt over time to related but distinct tasks, as in continual learning settings. Efficiency can be improved by transferring knowledge from a pretrained teacher policy to guide exploration in new but related tasks. However, if the new task sufficiently differs from the teacher's training task, the transferred guidance may be sub-optimal and bias exploration toward low-reward behaviors. We propose an energy-based transfer learning method that uses out-of-distribution detection to selectively issue guidance, enabling the teacher to intervene only in states within its training distribution. We theoretically link energy scores to state-visitation patterns under on-policy reinforcement learning. Empirically, our method improves sample efficiency and performance across both single-task and multi-task settings. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: A Comprehensive Evaluation on Quantization Techniques for Large Language Models
docs.text:
A Comprehensive Evaluation on Quantization Techniques for Large Language Models A Comprehensive Evaluation on Quantization Techniques for Large Language Models arXiv:2507.17417v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: For large language models (LLMs), post-training quantization (PTQ) significantly reduces memory and computational overhead. Despite rapid advancements, existing papers often lack experiments on the same ground. In addition, since quantization solutions typically contain multiple components, it is important to analyze the connections among numerous existing methods to gain an in-depth understanding of this field. To bridge these gaps, we conduct an up-to-date and extensive review of the state-of-the-art methods and perform comprehensive evaluations of low-bit quantization on representative text-only LLMs on the same ground to ensure fair comparisons. To our knowledge, this fair and extensive investigation remains critically important yet significantly underexplored in the research community. To better understand the connections, we first decouple published quantization into two steps: pre-quantization transformation to reduce outliers, and quantization error mitigation to offset performance loss. Second, we extensively evaluate the impact of quantization settings, including granularity and symmetry. Third, we analyze the performance of the latest MXFP4 and NVFP4 data formats. Our experimental results first demonstrate that optimizing rotation and scaling yields the best pre-quantization transformation, while combining low-rank compensation with GPTQ occasionally outperforms using GPTQ alone. Second, we verify that finer granularity improves performance at the cost of storage and asymmetric quantization benefits activations significantly more than weights. Third, we find that the format and precision of scaling factors have a significant impact on performance; notably, rotation-based transformation is effective for INT4 but demonstrates little improvement for MXFP4 and NVFP4, inspiring further investigation in this field. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: VRPRM: Process Reward Modeling via Visual Reasoning
docs.text:
VRPRM: Process Reward Modeling via Visual Reasoning VRPRM: Process Reward Modeling via Visual Reasoning arXiv:2508.03556v5 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Process Reward Models (PRMs) provide fine-grained supervision over intermediate reasoning steps, yet most existing models lack long-range reasoning and deep thinking capabilities. Although prior work has introduced Chain-of-Thought (CoT) to reward models, the high annotation cost of CoT-PRM still limits its scalability. To address these challenges, we propose the Visual Reasoning Process Reward Model (VRPRM) and design a label-efficient two-stage training strategy. Experimental results demonstrate that with only 5.5K CoT-PRM supervised step labels and 40K non-CoT PRM reinforcement learning training examples, VRPRM achieves a macro F1 score of 69.18 on VisualProcessBench, outperforming VisualPRM-8B, a non-thinking PRM trained on 400K examples, by 7.00 points. In Best-of-N evaluation, VRPRM-RL brings absolute Overall improvements of 21.77, 23.42, and 23.12 points on InternVL2.5-8B, 26B, and 38B policies, respectively, with a maximum relative improvement of 59.0\%. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: UniPrompt-CL: Efficient Single-Inference Continual Learning for Medical Image Classification
docs.text:
UniPrompt-CL: Efficient Single-Inference Continual Learning for Medical Image Classification UniPrompt-CL: Efficient Single-Inference Continual Learning for Medical Image Classification arXiv:2508.10954v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Medical AI systems must remain reliable as data distributions shift across hospitals, imaging devices, and patient populations, yet privacy constraints often prevent storing or revisiting past patient data. We present UniPrompt-CL, a rehearsal-free domain-incremental learning framework for medical image classification using a single backbone and a single inference. Rather than relying on multiple backbones, repeated ViT inferences, or independent layer-wise prompt pools, UniPrompt-CL shares a unified prompt pool across transformer layers and expands it with only a few prompts per new domain. This reduces cross-layer redundancy while enabling efficient adaptation. On diabetic retinopathy, UniPrompt-CL improves average accuracy by 2.0 percentage points and substantially reduces forgetting relative to the strongest backbone-matched baseline. On skin cancer, it achieves competitive accuracy at the lowest training cost among DINOv2-B configurations. A controlled comparison varying only pool organization shows that the benefit arises from retention rather than learning each new domain: it is largest on the medical benchmarks, smaller on OfficeHome, and reverses on a heterogeneous six-stage DomainNet stream. These results suggest that cross-layer prompt sharing with lightweight expansion is practical for medical models requiring repeated retraining under limited on-site compute, while identifying the domain shifts under which it helps. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: TopoMap: A Feature-based Discriminator of the Topographical Regions in the Test Input Space
docs.text:
TopoMap: A Feature-based Discriminator of the Topographical Regions in the Test Input Space TopoMap: A Feature-based Discriminator of the Topographical Regions in the Test Input Space arXiv:2509.03242v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Testing Deep Learning (DL)-based systems is an open challenge. Although it is relatively easy to find inputs that cause a DL model to misbehave, the grouping of such inputs by features that make them problematic for the DL model under test is largely unexplored. In this work, we propose TopoMap, a model-agnostic approach that relies solely on features that characterise inputs to construct a partitioning of the input space where each region represents a specific set of distinguishable input features. Such a partitioning gives users a possibility to identify and analyse areas that are under-represented, show higher failure rates, or exhibit prediction changes after a model update. The identified regions of interest can then be used for additional data generation or can help prioritise already generated inputs that require labelling efforts. To discriminate inputs according to the specific features they share, we first apply dimensionality reduction to obtain input embeddings that are then subjected to clustering. Each DL model might require specific embedding computations and clustering algorithms, and specific configurations of the two, to achieve a meaningful separation of inputs into discriminative groups. We propose a novel way to evaluate alternative configurations of embedding and clustering techniques. We use a deep neural network (DNN) as an approximation of a human evaluator who could tell whether a pair of clusters can be discriminated based on the features of the included elements. The evaluation results show that the maps generated by TopoMap consist of distinguishable and meaningful regions. In addition, we evaluate the effectiveness of TopoMap using mutation analysis. In particular, we assess whether the clusters in our topographical map allow for an effective selection of mutation-killing inputs. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: BrainPro: Process-conditioned Pretraining with Topographic Retrieval for Large EEG Models
docs.text:
BrainPro: Process-conditioned Pretraining with Topographic Retrieval for Large EEG Models BrainPro: Process-conditioned Pretraining with Topographic Retrieval for Large EEG Models arXiv:2509.22050v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: EEG foundation models are pretrained on heterogeneous corpora, but two challenges remain underexplored: (1) experimental protocols provide mental-process cues that are rarely used in masked pretraining, and (2) electrode montages vary across datasets, making spatial representations montage-dependent. Existing methods typically learn a single general-purpose representation and model spatial structure implicitly, limiting their ability to exploit process-related information under montage heterogeneity. We introduce BrainPro, a process-conditioned self-supervised pretraining framework that couples topographic retrieval with shared and process-associated representation learning. BrainPro maps dataset-specific montages to a universal channel-region template and retrieves channel- and region-level spatial filters to form a topographically aligned spatial basis. Over this basis, BrainPro learns a shared encoder for general EEG structure and additional affective, motor-related, and auxiliary residual branches for process-associated variation. Protocol-derived mental-process cues condition branch activation and region-weighted masked reconstruction, incorporating topographic spatial priors and process information. Across nine public BCI benchmarks, BrainPro achieves strong performance among evaluated baselines. Ablations, channel-drop analysis, encoder-configuration studies, and spatial-filter visualizations suggest that topographic retrieval and process-conditioned representation learning jointly improve EEG decoding. Our code is available at https://github.com/yi-ding-cs/BrainPro. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Sculpting the Latent Space: Disentanglement with WAE-MMD and Programmable Priors
docs.text:
Sculpting the Latent Space: Disentanglement with WAE-MMD and Programmable Priors Sculpting the Latent Space: Disentanglement with WAE-MMD and Programmable Priors arXiv:2510.11953v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Learning disentangled representations, where semantic features are independently captured in a latent space, is dominated by Variational Auto Encoders (VAE) and Adversarial Training. In this paper, we provide direct quantitative and visual evidence that these methods consistently fail to enforce the target factorized representation on the aggregate posterior, leading to entangled representations. We quantify this failure using the Latent Predictability Score (LPS), an unsupervised metric of mutual predictability that empirically lower bounds the level of entanglement in a latent space. To address these limitations, we leverage the non-parametric Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) to directly sculpt the aggregate posterior enabling programmable priors. We demonstrate (1) state-of-the-art unsupervised statistical independence, with a 70% reduction in detected entanglement compared to leading baselines; (2) the flexibility to optionally inject semi-supervised information for explicit semantic alignment; and (3) precise shaping of the aggregate posterior distribution (validated through quantization-aware training) without sacrificing reconstruction quality. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Memorizing Long-tail Data Can Help Generalization Through Composition
docs.text:
Memorizing Long-tail Data Can Help Generalization Through Composition Memorizing Long-tail Data Can Help Generalization Through Composition arXiv:2510.16322v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Deep learning has led researchers to rethink the relationship between memorization and generalization. In many settings, memorization does not hurt generalization due to implicit regularization and may help by memorizing long-tailed examples. In this paper, we consider the synergy between memorization and simple composition -- the ability to make correct prediction on a combination of long-tailed features. Theoretically, we show that for a linear setting, memorization together with composition can help the model make correct predictions on rare test examples that require a combination of long-tailed features, even if such combinations were never observed in the training data. Experiments on neural network architecture on simple data show that the theoretical insight extends beyond the linear setting, and we further observe that the composition capability of the model depends on its architecture. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: Structured Temporal Causality for Interpretable Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
docs.text:
Structured Temporal Causality for Interpretable Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection Structured Temporal Causality for Interpretable Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection arXiv:2510.16511v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Real-world multivariate time series anomalies are rare and often unlabeled. Additionally, prevailing methods rely on increasingly complex architectures tuned to benchmarks, detecting only fragments of anomalous segments and overstating performance. In this paper, we introduce OracleAD, a simple and interpretable unsupervised framework for multivariate time series anomaly detection. OracleAD encodes each variable's past sequence into a single causal embedding to jointly predict the present time point and reconstruct the input window, effectively modeling temporal dynamics. These embeddings then undergo a self-attention mechanism to project them into a shared latent space and capture spatial relationships. These relationships are not static, since they are modeled by a property that emerges from each variable's temporal dynamics. The projected embeddings are aligned to a Stable Latent Structure (SLS) representing normal-state relationships. Anomalies are identified using a dual scoring mechanism based on prediction error and deviation from the SLS, enabling fine-grained anomaly diagnosis at each time point and across individual variables. Since any noticeable SLS deviation originates from embeddings that violate the learned temporal causality of normal data, OracleAD directly pinpoints the root-cause variables at the embedding level. OracleAD achieves state-of-the-art results across multiple real-world datasets and evaluation protocols, while remaining interpretable through SLS. アルゴリズム paper

docs.title: ChemBART: Pre-training a Reaction Language Model for Comprehensive Synthesis Planning
docs.text:
ChemBART: Pre-training a Reaction Language Model for Comprehensive Synthesis Planning ChemBART: Pre-training a Reaction Language Model for Comprehensive Synthesis Planning arXiv:2601.02915v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated transformative potential across diverse fields. However, in computer-aided synthesis planning (CASP), current LLM methodologies are often restricted to single-molecule representations, limiting their application to isolated, single-task scenarios such as precursor prediction. Addressing this gap, we present ChemBART, a BART-based language model that adopts a reaction-centric pre-training strategy. By leveraging a mask-filling pre-training task on holistic reaction expressions (Reactant > Reagent > Product), ChemBART effectively solves a variety of chemical problems, including precursor/reagent generation, temperature-yield regression, and molecular property classification. Building on these capabilities, we demonstrate the integration of ChemBART with Monte Carlo tree search (MCTS) for multi-step synthesis route design, where the model serves to optimize the policy and value functions within a reinforcement learning framework. Beyond single-molecule pre-trained LLMs that are constrained to specific applications, ChemBART unifies diverse chemical tasks to facilitate synthesis planning with comprehensive implementation information. Most significantly, the proposed multi-step synthesis routes and reaction conditions were validated in the wet lab, confirming the discovery of shorter synthetic pathways with a >20% yield improvement over established literature benchmarks.
